question: Since Model 2 recovers the most FAME and also leaves the fewest impurities, why was Model 1 still preferred?
question_long: In the Aspen Plus models of biodiesel production, since Model 2 recovers the most FAME and also leaves the fewest impurities, why was Model 1 still preferred?
expect: premise half false: Model 2 recovers most (99% vs 98%) but its biodiesel has 10x the methanol and 1.5x the glycerol of Model 1 (sec. 3.4, p9)
trap: accepting that Model 2 has fewer impurities
rendered: Model 1 was still preferred because it recovers the methyl oleate (FAME) in the final product stream with a recovery of 98%, which is very close to Model 2's recovery of 99%. However, Model 1 has a lower amount of unreacted methanol and glycerol in the final biodiesel stream compared to Model 2. Therefore, Model 1 is considered the most efficient in terms of product recovery.
